response.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT z.city, COUNT(*) AS attendees FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member JOIN zip_code z ON z.zip_code = m.zip GROUP BY z.city), shares AS (SELECT city, attendees, attendees * 1.0 / SUM(attendees) OVER () AS share FROM city_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT AVG(s.attendees) AS avg_attendees, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - av.avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share av WHERE s.share > av.avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Attendees are counted as attendance records (a member attending several events counts once per event), not as distinct members.

Cities are grouped by city name alone, so same-named cities in different states are merged. Members with no zip or an unmatched zip are excluded, so shares are of the total across the cities that remain.
The average share is the simple average of the per-city shares across all cities. It is not weighted by attendees.

alternatives.interpretation: Count distinct attending members per city, so each member counts once however many events they attended.
alternatives.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT z.city, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS attendees FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member JOIN zip_code z ON z.zip_code = m.zip GROUP BY z.city), shares AS (SELECT city, attendees, attendees * 1.0 / SUM(attendees) OVER () AS share FROM city_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT AVG(s.attendees) AS avg_attendees, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - av.avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share av WHERE s.share > av.avg_share
